title: Remember Future Cop: LAPD? Remember tower defense and MOBAs? Remember seeing flowers? Hex Tower Boogie somehow combines all of that, and it's in the upcoming Steam Next Fest
author: Designer-Rain6712
selftext:
**Hi! We're 3ofUs from Saxony, Germany, and we want to show you our wild mix: Hex Tower Boogie.**

We remember playing Future Cop: LAPD on the PlayStation 1 back in 1998. Then came tower defense on the school PC, on sites like Kongregate in the 2000s. And then League of Legends ate several years of our dwindling youth.

Now, two decades later, with the power of AI and a lot of nostalgia, we gave it a go. At the beginning of the year we built a 2D tower defense, got it almost ready to ship, and scrapped everything. Half a year later we're in Steam Next Fest, in 3D.

**What is Hex Tower Boogie?**

Four players, free for all or 2 vs 2. Your goal is to get your minions into the enemy base, and the further they get, the more gold they earn you. On defense you have our main piece: the pipeline to your towers, with our own trigger and effect system.

**What's the trigger and effect system?**

You build your ammo yourself. Every bullet has two parts, a trigger and an effect:

\- \[OnHit\](Damage) is the most basic bullet.

\- \[OnShoot\](Multishot) + \[OnHit\](Damage): two effects on one bullet, each with its own trigger.

\- More triggers? \[OnShoot\]\[OnKill\](Multishot) + \[OnHit\](Damage).

\- Chain reaction? \[OnShoot\](Multishot) + \[OnHit\](Splash). Yes, that's multiple splashes.

**How we used AI**

We built a system of gates that every worktree has to pass. The code is written with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code. Before any code is written in a worktree, Claude Fable checks the plan and improves it. When the work is done, Fable checks the worktree again, this time focused on how to fit it cleanly into the rest of the project. In the very last step we check the code with Astra for a second opinion. In almost every case, each of these three review rounds improved the code or the idea we were trying to build.

For the 3D models we used Blender through its MCP connection: Claude did the modeling and Astra did the texture work. That worked quite well.

Before Next Fest starts on Monday we want to test in a public round and build a community. There's still a lot to fine tune, improve, explain and build. What confuses you in your first match? Is the ammo system readable?

Be one of the very first players of Hex Tower Boogie:
